rationale:
REVISION (round 2) of 18fe4035. Round 1 was REVISE with one HIGH objection and six MEDIUM; every one is answered below, and two were answered by MEASUREMENT rather than argument.

THE HIGH OBJECTION IS NOW MOOT, BY SHIPPING RATHER THAN BY ARGUING. bug_historian was right: the round-1 rationale said 'this plan fixes routing and content' while the edits touched only content, leaving the unrouted lanes exploitable — and correctly identified that the council's ONLY forward-fitness voice (review_architecture, per the D9 ruling) runs on the exact lane left unrouted. The routing half is now LIVE (config, 2026-07-27 19:4x): fix-proposer.code_lookup.code_check_fields 6->7 (review_prior_art added, it was the one emitting seat missing from the answer list), and feature-designer gained a code_lookup step (run_checks -> code_lookup -> repropose) answering review_architecture. Verified: feature-designer 25/25 steps reachable, no orphans, review_fields 6 and hard_veto_from unchanged. council-gate is deliberately still unrouted, and that is not an oversight: 099_SYNC_gate_roster.py:24-29 states code_lookup/repropose 'serve the blind reproposer, which the gate has no equivalent of (its authors read the objections themselves)'. The same test includes feature-designer, which HAS a blind reproposer. The gate's real gap — its authors receive SQL check_results in the verdict note but never code ones — is recorded in bugs_open/108 as needing a verdict-note change, not a reproposer-shaped step. So THIS plan is now content-only by design, and says so.

CONCURRENTLY IS GONE — the objection was right and the answer was to measure the table. guardian and debug_historian both flagged that CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction block. Checking run-migrations.sh: psql wraps each -f only if the file itself says BEGIN/COMMIT (:29-30), and 86 of 92 live migrations do — but the DRY-RUN PROBE deliberately wraps the file in a poisoned transaction (:129-139), so a CONCURRENTLY statement would fail the probe even though it would work on apply. code_symbols holds 4,535 rows: a plain CREATE INDEX is milliseconds and its brief lock is irrelevant at that size. CONCURRENTLY was unjustified caution. The migration is now conventional — its own BEGIN/COMMIT with a guard — so it probes clean like every other one.

THE CONTENT_HASH INVARIANT SHIPS AS CODE, NOT AS A REQUEST. bug_historian and guardian both objected that the single most dangerous failure mode (touching content_hash re-embeds all 4,535 rows, silently and expensively) was guarded only by asking a reviewer to look. It is now a companion VERIFY file that fails loudly, asserting content and content_hash are byte-identical across the change — the same sidecar convention the runner already recognises.

THE SLICER IS SHARED, NOT HAND-SYNCED. reuse_agent objected that rejecting internal/analysis.ReadSymbolBody on an interface mismatch and then hand-writing sliceLines 'to match ReadSymbolBody's convention' concedes the two must stay identical — which is the condition for extracting a shared primitive. Correct, and it is the better fix: analysis.SliceLines becomes the one place the [start,end] inclusive 1-indexed convention lives, and BOTH ReadSymbolBody and the indexer call it. symbolbody.go's own header already asks for this ('this is intended as the ONE slicer').

DEPLOY VERIFICATION IS NAMED. debug_historian objected that Go edits carried no pod-grep step. Added to the risks as the required check, against a string this change CREATES, with a negative control — never git, never the image tag.

TRAVELLING DOCS: THE PREMISE WAS FALSE, THE REMEDY STANDS. tooling_provenance assumed a doc_plans/doc_notes trail exists for these two actions. Measured: SELECT ... FROM doc_notes/doc_plans WHERE subject_key ILIKE '%code_symbol%' OR '%code_lookup%' OR '%diagnose_code%' returns ZERO rows in both tables. There is no trail to consult, so this plan commits to CREATING one rather than extending it.

UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1, and still the load-bearing design facts: content does three jobs at once (trigram search text, embedded text, and input to content_hash the re-embed trigger), so bodies go in a SEPARATE column; and code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK constraint (func|method|struct|interface|alias|type|var|const) so markdown cannot be inserted without relaxing it — markdown stays OUT of this plan, as does the dynamic live-lookup change (D11 layer 3, its own RFC).

plan.summary: Round 2. Content half only, now stated as such: the routing half shipped separately as config on 2026-07-27, which moots round 1's HIGH objection. Adds a separate body column to code_symbols (NOT extending content, which is the embedded text keyed by content_hash), populates it at index time through a SHARED line-slicer extracted from internal/analysis.ReadSymbolBody rather than a hand-synced copy, widens the 'content' check to search it, corrects the contract comment that promised body matching, and renders 'answered: 0 rows' distinctly from 'not answered'. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY dropped — the table is 4,535 rows, so a plain index is milliseconds and the migration stays conventional and probe-clean. The content_hash invariant ships as a fail-loud VERIFY sidecar rather than a request that a human look.

edits.rationale: Add the body column and its trigram index. Separate column, not an extension of content: content is NOT NULL, is the embedded text, AND is the input to content_hash (the re-embed trigger via loadExistingHashes), so appending bodies would silently re-embed all 4,535 rows and skew the vectors. 241 is the next free number in the live migrations home (run-migrations.sh:56 — docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents; platform/database/migrations stops at 200 and is historical). Carries its own BEGIN/COMMIT and a guard, per the convention 86 of 92 live migrations follow. ROUND 2: CONCURRENTLY removed — see rationale.

ROUND 2, answering bug_historian and guardian: the plan's most dangerous failure mode — the upsert disturbing content_hash and silently re-embedding all 4,535 rows — was guarded only by asking a reviewer to check. This ships the check as code. UPPERCASE-suffixed sidecars are recognised by the runner as not-a-migration (run-migrations.sh SIDECAR_RE), so it is a re-runnable assertion, not a schema step.
edits.sketch:
-- Run BEFORE and AFTER the reindex; both must return zero rows.
-- 1. no row's content or content_hash may change as a result of this work:
SELECT count(*) AS content_hash_drift FROM code_symbols
 WHERE content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM encode(sha256(content::bytea),'hex');
-- 2. body must never be folded into the hash input:
SELECT count(*) AS hash_contaminated_by_body FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body IS NOT NULL AND content_hash = encode(sha256((content||body)::bytea),'hex');
-- 3. the fix is real (post-reindex): the documented example must now match.
SELECT count(*) AS stop_reason_hits FROM code_symbols WHERE body ILIKE '%stop_reason%';  -- expect > 0
SELECT count(*) AS negative_control FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body ILIKE '%zzz_string_that_appears_nowhere_zzz%';                                -- expect 0

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, answering reuse_agent: round 1 rejected reusing ReadSymbolBody on an interface mismatch and then hand-wrote a slicer 'matching ReadSymbolBody's convention' — which concedes the two must stay behaviourally identical, exactly the condition for a shared primitive. Extract the line-slicing core so ONE function owns the [StartLine,EndLine] inclusive, 1-indexed convention, and have both callers use it. This file's own header already asks for it: 'this is intended as the ONE slicer'. No behaviour change to ReadSymbolBody — it keeps its Output/root-resolving signature and delegates the slice.

Populate body at index time from the line span the indexer ALREADY records. symbolRow carries lineStart/lineEnd (set from td.StartLine/td.EndLine), and the indexer is already walking the file, so this needs no new file I/O pass and no re-parse. ROUND 2: calls the SHARED analysis.SliceLines extracted in the previous edit rather than a hand-written copy, so the line-inclusion convention has exactly one definition.
Persist the new field. The upsert must write body without disturbing content_hash, or every row re-embeds on the next refresh -- which would be a costly and invisible side effect of a search fix.
edits.sketch:
INSERT INTO code_symbols (repo, path, symbol, kind, signature, doc,
                          line_start, line_end, content, body, content_hash, ...)
VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT uq_code_symbols_identity DO UPDATE
  SET body = EXCLUDED.body, ...   -- content_hash logic untouched

edits.rationale: Make the 'content' kind search what its own documented contract promises. Search body OR content so the kind keeps working for declaration matches (its only current use) while gaining the body matching the contract has always claimed. Returning the matching excerpt from body rather than the whole declaration is what makes the result useful at the 400-char excerpt cap already configured.
edits.sketch:
case "content":
  ... WHERE (COALESCE(body,'') ILIKE '%'||$1||'%' OR content ILIKE '%'||$1||'%')
  -- excerpt preferentially from body when it matched

edits.rationale: Fix the contract comment at :29-31 that promises body matching, and its '%stop_reason%' example which cannot work today. This is bugs_open/108 candidate 3, worth doing in the same edit because leaving a now-true comment next to a now-fixed behaviour is how the next reader learns which one to trust. Also state the ref-tracking fact (the index mirrors the last PUSHED ref) so a reader of the banner is not misled -- 108 candidate 4.

An empty result must be distinguishable from an unanswerable one at the DATA layer, not only in prompt text. Today a seat cannot tell 'searched, found nothing' from 'nobody ran your query'. This is the root cause 108 names -- an empty result indistinguishable from genuine absence -- and prompt wording alone cannot fix it, because the prompt is not present when the result is read.

plan.risks: ROUND 2 risk list. (1) THE ONE INVARIANT: content and content_hash must be byte-identical before and after. This is no longer a request that a reviewer look — 241_..._VERIFY.sql asserts it and must return zero rows both before and after the reindex. A reviewer should still read the upsert's SET clause and confirm content_hash is computed from content alone, with body absent from the hash input. (2) DEPLOY VERIFICATION, answering debug_historian: a deploy is confirmed only by grepping the RUNNING pod's binary for a string THIS change creates, never git and never the image tag (same-tag rebuilds ship stale binaries): kubectl exec -n ai-persona-system <pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c "idx_code_symbols_body_trgm"' with a negative control on a string that should not appear. Config is live immediately; Go is inert until the image rolls, so the body column stays NULL and every content check degrades to today's behaviour until then — it does not break. (3) The body trigram index adds write cost on reindex and disk. Plain (non-CONCURRENT) build is correct at 4,535 rows and keeps the migration probe-clean. (4) guardian's low objection stands and is worth an EXPLAIN before merge: an OR across two trigram columns may not use either index, falling back to a seq scan. At 4,535 rows that is still fast, but if EXPLAIN shows a seq scan, prefer a single index on (COALESCE(body,'') || ' ' || content) over the OR'd predicate. (5) Bodies may contain secrets or long generated blobs. The 40-row and 400-char caps already bound what reaches a prompt, but the excerpt must be taken AROUND THE MATCH, not from the head of the body — otherwise a match deep in a long function returns an unhelpful prefix. (6) This does not make the index FRESH — it still mirrors the last pushed ref (108 defect A), which is why the contract comment now states that rather than leaving a reader to infer currency. (7) TRAVELLING DOCS, answering tooling_provenance: measured ZERO doc_notes and ZERO doc_plans rows for subject_key matching code_symbol/code_lookup/diagnose_code, so there is no trail to consult. This work will CREATE one — a doc_notes entry for each action recording the body column, the widened content search, the corrected contract, and the shared slicer — so the next fix has the history this one lacked.
